summary: Reid Hoffman argues NVIDIA's AI chip dominance is sustainable for at least two more years, and explicitly advises against shorting the stock, though he sees margin pressure emerging from inference competition in the medium term.
quote: NVIDIA has a very sharp, you know, kind of lead on the importance of the chips for the training clusters... I would recommend people not be short on NVIDIA.

summary: Reid Hoffman praises Satya Nadella as the best public-market CEO of his generation, highlighting his disciplined blend of strategic AI platform investment with return-on-capital discipline, positioning Microsoft well for the AI era.
quote: I think Satya is like the best public market CEO of our generation. I think he is stunning in kind of blending combination of strategic insight with also kind of being, you know, kind of return on capital, you know, sensible risk-taking.

summary: Reid Hoffman identifies Apple's App Store as the prime antitrust target among big tech, arguing its mandatory fees and sideloading ban quell startup innovation and create anti-competitive dynamics that merit regulatory intervention.
quote: I actually frankly think that the prime candidate is likely to be, and I'm speaking as an individual and as a venture capitalist here, is Apple with the App Store.
